keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the ground surface — not just straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you may count. Within 50 m of a tall man-made obstacle (over 105 m), the party responsible for the obstacle may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

The operator must normally be registered if the drone weighs at least 250 g or is fitted with a camera or sensor capable of collecting personal data, unless it is covered by the toy exemption. Requirements regarding drone licences and flight distances depend on the drone’s class, weight and sub-category.

In Sweden, you must be 15 years old to fly independently with an A1/A3 drone certificate (online theory test with Transportstyrelsen, subject to a fee, valid for 5 years). Anyone under 15 may only fly under the direct supervision of a remote pilot who is at least 16 years old and holds a valid drone certificate themselves.
The operator number must be clearly marked on the drone.

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your own unaided visual line of sight (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, with clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can scan the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
A1: Drones weighing less than 250 g — may be flown over uninvolved people, but never over crowds.
A2: Drones weighing up to 4 kg — at least 30 m from uninvolved people (5 m with low-speed mode activated, ≤ 3 m/s) and always at least the flight height (the 1:1 rule). Requires an A2 certificate.
A3: Drones weighing up to 25 kg — fly only where no uninvolved people are expected to be present, and at least 150 m horizontally from residential, commercial, industrial, and recreational areas.
Never fly over crowds without special permission.
Check the LFV Drone Map and NOTAMs before each flight.
importantNotes: As of January 1, 2026, it is a criminal offense to fly a drone weighing 250 g or more without a valid drone license—punishable by a fine or up to six months in prison.
Nature reserves and national parks often have their own restrictions—check with the County Administrative Board for the specific area.

Protected sites may be subject to access and photography restrictions and may also be located within a restricted area. Check signage, official decisions and the latest airspace information for the location.

Anyone operating a drone must report incidents in which someone has been seriously injured, a fatal accident has occurred, or a manned aircraft has been involved. Other requirements may apply to activities subject to authorisation. The Swedish Transport Agency also encourages the voluntary reporting of other safety incidents.
Insurance is strongly recommended—some home insurance policies cover drone flights, while others do not.
